1 review finding open, listed at the end.

No configuration clears both gates: the two that hold a 97% pass rate in every task run past the 600 ms latency budget, and every one inside the budget misses the pass rate, always on multi-hop.

Brisk-S with high reasoning and a retry holds the pass rate everywhere, its thinnest task 0.3 points over the gate, but reaches 870 ms at p95. A budget that admits it, or a low-reasoning configuration that fixes multi-hop, would change the answer.

!
Pass rates over all tasks, as the options table prints them, are not the gate: it reads each task. Latency was measured only over all tasks, so every latency verdict here is inferred from the overall p95.
!
Confidence: High, if the caveats below aren't material.
  • No arm is the control. Only for the claim that Brisk-S and Atlas-M at high reasoning with a retry are not told apart: with no control they compare unpaired, which reads wider than a paired test would. The finding that nothing clears both gates compares no two configurations.
  • The pick is the best of several candidates. Only for Brisk-S with high reasoning and a retry clearing multi-hop by 0.3 points: as the best of 18 configurations it likely reads high, so a fresh run would more likely put it under the gate, which still leaves nothing clearing both.
  • Per-task latency unmeasured. Only if a configuration inside the budget over all tasks also cleared the pass rate; none does today. For the two that hold the pass rate, a p95 over all tasks past the budget means at least one task is past it too, provided each case belongs to one task.
  • Task pass rates state no count. Only if Brisk-S with low reasoning and a retry truly clears multi-hop and ambiguous entities. Under counts assumed from traffic shares, a run of today's size reads its multi-hop miss the wrong way 11.9% of the time and its ambiguous-entity miss 33.3%, and its date-math figure sits exactly on the gate. To clear both gates it would need both misses and the date-math reading to land on the passing side together, and its unmeasured per-task latency to stay within 600 ms. The counts are assumed, so the true spread could be wider than these chances suggest.
What is tangledThe pass-rate gate and the latency budget pull against each other through the reasoning setting. Both configurations that hold the pass rate everywhere use high reasoning, which puts p95 past the budget. The closest one inside the budget, Brisk-S with low reasoning and a retry (513 ms at p95), misses the pass rate on multi-hop by 1.4 points and on ambiguous entities by 0.6.
What we know despite itOf the two that hold the pass rate, Brisk-S with high reasoning and a retry is not told apart from Atlas-M with the same settings (-0.7 points, interval -1.7 to +0.4), and Atlas-M costs 5.5 times as much per 1,000 calls at this run's routing.
Our leanOurs, not a call: if the latency owner can accept a per-task budget that covers Brisk-S with high reasoning and a retry in its slowest task, it is the configuration to confirm. That budget is at least 870 ms, its p95 over all tasks, and likely more on multi-hop; the exact figure stays unknown until per-task latency is measured. Under today's budget, nothing measured qualifies.
WatchBrisk-S with high reasoning and a retry clears every task on its point estimate alone. Under counts assumed from traffic shares, a run of today's size would read it under the gate 37.4% of the time on multi-hop, 29.9% on ambiguous entities, 16.5% on date math and 0.3% on single lookups.
What would settle itPer-task p95 latency for the two Brisk-S configurations with a retry, and a declaration from the latency owner on whether the per-task budget is firm.

Left out, and why

Monthly cost at the declared volume
The declared volume does not say what it counts, so a monthly figure could be off by the calls each unit holds; cost is given per 1,000 calls.
Nano-XS per-task figures
Every Nano-XS configuration misses the gate in every task; the best reads 94.8% over all tasks. They stay in the full tables, and none is among the configurations nearest the gate.
What the retry buys on its own
It lifts pass rate at every reasoning level, with intervals that barely clear zero on a descriptive read; both configurations near the gate already use it, so it does not choose between them.
Model and retry interactions across the grid (the retry helps Nano-XS more than Atlas-M)
Nano-XS is far from the gate in every configuration; the interaction does not change which configurations come close.
Calls per task, extra calls and outcome
Extra calls and outcome hold no figures; calls per task describes the planner's work, not either gate.
Failure examples
The snapshot keeps none.

Method

Cases
1,200 planner tasks per configuration, none lost, across four tasks: single lookup (40% of traffic), multi-hop (25%), date and unit math (20%) and ambiguous entity (15%). No repeats are stated.
Pass
The snapshot does not state what makes a planner task pass; pass rate is the share of tasks it counts as passed.
Gates
Declared: a pass rate of at least 97% in each task, and p95 latency of at most 600 ms in each task. Both are read as gates on the point estimate; a configuration with no figure at a place a gate reads is undecided there, not failed. A pass rate over all tasks is shown for reference only and is never the gate.

Caveats: Per-task latency unmeasured.

Intervals
Overall pass-rate intervals are computed from each configuration's cases (binomial, at the level the tables print); differences between configurations combine the two unpaired and are descriptive. Task pass rates state no count, so they carry no interval; run sizes for them assume each task holds its traffic share of the cases.

Caveats: Task pass rates state no count.

Latency
p50 and p95 over all tasks, with no interval; no per-task latency is held in the snapshot, and whether the run kept per-case timings is not stated.
Cost
Cost per 1,000 calls as measured in this run. The snapshot names each configuration's model but no provider, so the routing behind each cost, and behind each latency, is unknown. The declared volume, 4,000,000 a month, does not say what it counts.
Comparison
Eighteen configurations crossing three models, three reasoning levels and a retry; no control, so every comparison is between two configurations' own figures.

Caveats: No arm is the control.

Source
Synthetic example data from docs/eval-report-kit/references/r2-config-sweep.json
